title: Introducing Claude Ship
summary: Claude Ship is a system for moving pull requests through review, fixes, and approval, combining Code Review (now GA) with the beta PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Claude repairs failing checks, merge conflicts, and reviewer feedback, and approves changes that a policy file permits, while /ship in Claude Code advances your own PRs once admins enable it per GitHub repo on Team and Enterprise plans. It is token-billed with admin spend limits, is unavailable with ZDR, HIPAA configuration, or customer-managed keys, and aims to remove the review and merge bottleneck as agents write more code.

title: Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in beta
summary: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), a misuse-detection layer that works with zero data retention, has moved from private beta with 100+ customers to public beta. It is available on Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud, with Microsoft Foundry coming. Customers keep inputs and outputs in their own cloud, while automated cross-request monitoring detects coordinated attacks that look harmless per request.

title: Linked billing on the Claude Platform
summary: Linked billing is a beta feature that lets end customers of third-party tools pay for their Claude API usage without sharing an API key. Customers link their Claude Platform org through a hosted flow, approve each platform, set spend limits, and can unlink at any time, while platforms see per-customer usage and choose who pays per request. Requests run in the platform's org, so customer-org IP allowlists, encryption keys, and retention settings do not apply, but the approach reduces key-handling risk and lets platforms ship Claude features without building billing.

title: The enterprise guide to securing coding agents
summary: This guide covers securing coding agents like Claude Code against leaked credentials, unvetted dependencies and extensions, data exfiltration, and prompt injection, with six questions for vetting providers. It describes layered defenses: a judgment layer (alignment, probes, auto mode classifier) and fixed boundaries (permissions, hooks, sandboxing, egress allowlists) that can be centrally locked. Auto mode is now the default for interactive sessions on every plan, skill and plugin scanning is available on Enterprise, and Salesforce is cited at 79% more PRs merged per developer and 5% fewer incidents.

title: KPMG's Todd Lohr on AI when your data is also your clients' data
summary: An Anthropic interview with KPMG US Vice Chair Todd Lohr covers adopting frontier AI while protecting client data. KPMG integrated Claude into its Digital Gateway tax platform, now called Digital Gateway Powered by Claude, and regulated-data firms can keep data in their own infrastructure and still use frontier models. Lohr's takeaway is that you have to adopt and secure at the same time, supported by Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (public beta) for misuse detection compatible with zero data retention.

title: The Claude Tag guide for startups
summary: A guide shows how eight fast-growing startups use Claude Tag, a beta Slack tool for @mentioning Claude, connecting tools, and assigning tasks. Use cases include alert triage, turning Slack threads into draft PRs, docs and code Q&A, self-serve data answers, and scheduled reports, with reported results such as a Slack mention opening a PR in 21 minutes. It stresses human review before merge, scoped access, and spend limits, and is available only on Claude Team and Enterprise plans.
